title: Mini-app packs — family normative contract (apiVersion 1)
status: ratified — ADR-0029 accepted 2026-10-08 (with the s0GapResolutions folded into acceptance); apiVersion 1

derivation.singleSource: This document is the single normative source. The SDK validator (src/shared/app-pack/) and the runtime validator (src/main/apps/contract/) are both DERIVED from these vocabularies and share one implementation; parity is test-enforced. Drift between authoring and enforcement is a regression (ADR-0029 clause 11).
derivation.generatedArtifacts: Never hand-edit generated validators against this file; regenerate or align in the same commit.
derivation.manifestSchema: The FULL manifest serialization schema is an S1 deliverable: authored in the same commit as the one zod validator (runtime) and the SDK builders it validates, as a sibling artifact mini-app-packs.manifest.schema.json, derived from this file's vocabularies + manifestFieldMap, with SDK/runtime rejection-parity tests. Deliberately not written at S0: it must be derived from the implemented validator, not frozen ahead of it.

apiVersion.policy: Packs carry an integer apiVersion. A runtime accepts packs with apiVersion <= its own; older majors run under documented deprecation windows (window: deprecationWindowMajors); a pack with apiVersion > current self-disables at registration with reason 'requires host apiVersion >= N'. Unknown step/field/capability/slot anywhere in the manifest self-disables with a path-precise reason — packs never half-run (ADR-0029 clause 2).
apiVersion.evolution: Append-only within a major: NEW optional manifest fields, slot ids, capability ids, error codes, action ids, components and operators may be added WITHOUT bumping apiVersion (older hosts ignore unknown-to-them optionals per field policy; newer hosts accept older packs). Removing or re-semanticizing anything bumps the integer.

identity.uniqueness: Pack ids are unique per install. Importing a manifest whose id collides with a DIFFERENT installed pack is rejected with a typed reason. Re-importing the same id is the upgrade path: version must increase, the install is replaced, and verdicts invalidate via the packVersion cache key.

kind.assessment: A scan→verdict pipeline pack (run pipeline REQUIRED, propose optional).
kind.surface: A UI-contribution pack with NO run pipeline (pipeline FORBIDDEN) — launcher input modes, tools, panels.

identity.tierProvenance: Tier is install-time provenance, never manifest data: imported declarative manifest = Tier 0; bundled reviewed code shipped with the host = Tier 1; imported code = Tier 2 (deferred, unimplemented).

capabilities.grants: File metadata (path, name, ext, size, mtime) and — only when privacy.sendsContent is true and a step declares readContext — capped content excerpts, strictly inside the run's root allowlist.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Every path resolves inside the run root (see fs.rootValidation and fs.scanTraversal). Traversal, mount/device escape and refused roots are re-validated per call. Packs hold no OS handles.

capabilities.grants: The single destructive verb of apiVersion 1: move-to-quarantine. Executed ONLY by the host propose executor after HITL Class-B approval, per-item-atomic (see quarantine.move).
capabilities.hostEnforced: The pack declares the proposal; it never writes. Stale/changed items drop to 'ask'. Quarantine layout, retention and restore are host-owned (see quarantine).

capabilities.grants: Closed mutation verbs (rename, move) with a mandatory undo journal, HITL-armed, host-executed. Required by batch-renamer-class packs; a v1 validator REJECTS it with a precise 'requires contract apiVersion >= 2' reason (never a generic failure).

capabilities.status: reserved — denied in Tier 0, unimplemented in v1 (plan 26 non-goal)
capabilities.grants: Nothing in v1. Present in the vocabulary so a pack declaring it is rejected with the exfiltration-class reason, not an unknown-capability reason. Where a cloud engine is used, only the AI-layer engine transport leaves the device, never pack-controlled requests (ADR-0029 clause 6).
Atomic typed questions (noul/choice/score — the ADR-0019 neutral vocabulary, DecisionQuestion) on residual items only, via the host decision-engine registry.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Binds to task assignments through the existing engine registry (jev/needle/llm stay user-swappable); never a provider, model id or SDK. Every call is one AiCall audit row under the decision funnel; budgeted; concurrency-governed yielding to interactive calls. An optional per-pack engine preference is plain validated config.

capabilities.grants: Model I/O through host funnels: structured prompt→response via the gateway and sanctioned service funnels, schema-validated outputs.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Task-bound at call time by host config (chat-family or a sanctioned service funnel such as translation) — a pack never names a provider, model id, endpoint or SDK. Audited + budgeted like every gateway call. Used for synthesis/summaries — verdicts come from rules + the decide step, never from free-form llm output.

capabilities.grants: Lifecycle of the pack's OWN runs through the run bridge: start, progress, cancel, resume.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Checkpointed (see pipeline.run), budget pre-flight, boot reconciliation of orphaned runs. A pack can never address another pack's runs.

capabilities.grants: A declarative report UI schema rendered by the host from the closed component vocabulary (see report.components).
capabilities.hostEnforced: Actions are closed typed ids (see report.actions). Raw HTML/JS from packs is never rendered at any tier.

capabilities.grants: HITL Class-B arming declarations (ADR-0015): proposal cards grouped by category with per-item escalation, plus the fail-closed gate declaration.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Implements the full ADR-0015 Tier 1 floor: detached Class-B cards, idempotent resolve (second responder = no-op), conflict = rebase-or-reject (a stale item drops to 'ask'), resolution feedback, notification fanout. Arming is an explicit user act; execution re-validates every item and performs the mutation in the same main-side operation; side effects arm only from the user's act, never from model output.

capabilities.grants: Code-tier slot contributions into the fixed slot taxonomy (see slots).
capabilities.hostEnforced: The host supplies props and handlers and renders the contribution; no DOM injection, no free positioning; theme tokens, a11y bar and in-flow growth rules apply (see slots.globalRules). Tier 0 packs get their surfaces declaratively (report schema, settings auto-form, command registration) without this capability.

capabilities.grants: Full custom surfaces beyond slots — a trusted-tier (bundled-code-only) privilege.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Never importable. Review-required; any imported manifest declaring it is rejected.

capabilities.grants: A routed declarative page the host renders from the closed component vocabulary (plan 32 Phase 4 / ADR-0040 clause 16 — the declarative renderer lives in @neuronection/assistant-ui).
capabilities.hostEnforced: The host validates the declared surface schema against the charter components (deep validation desktop-side stays delegated to the mini-app surface laws) and renders it under family tokens; raw HTML/JS from packs is never rendered at any tier.

capabilities.grants: An embeddable declarative block inside a fixed host slot.
capabilities.hostEnforced: Same closed vocabulary; the host owns placement (no DOM injection, no free positioning).

capabilities.grants: A host-owned OS window rendering the pack's declared declarative surface (report/page) — Electron BrowserWindow on desktop, browser window/tab on web hosts, pywebview child on study.
capabilities.hostEnforced: The window is constrained: no node integration in the window, family tokens + the a11y bar, a per-pack window cap, and the kill switch closes it. An unhonored surface degrades along the charter degrade rules (window → page → panel) — the compat check is data, never code.

killSwitches.master: config.miniApps master switch (toolApps parity): off = no pack surfaces, no runs, no proposals.
killSwitches.perPack: Every installed pack has an enable switch independent of self-disable state; a disabled pack shows its surfaced reason and runs nothing.
killSwitches.arming: Aborting an armed batch is always available: not-yet-moved items return to 'ask', already-moved items stay restorable. Kill switches abort armed batches first (plan 26 S6).

slots.globalRules: All slot contributions obey family theme tokens, the axe a11y bar, and the host's in-flow growth rules (no fixed-position popups — they clip at window bounds); any native picker is wrapped in the host dialogGuard. Contribution ids are auto-namespaced '<packId>:<id>' so two packs can never collide. When multiple packs contribute to one slot, contributions compose in a stable host-owned order (bundled packs first, then install order); packs never see each other's contributions.

taxonomy.placement: Command catalog / palette entries that open or start the pack's surfaces.
taxonomy.packSupplies: Entry metadata (id, title key, icon spec, keywords, action binding).
taxonomy.hostSupplies: Catalog registration, palette rendering, execution funnel, history/attribution.

taxonomy.placement: A focused launcher mode that takes over the composer input with live results (the plan-14 §9 mini-app mode; accent border, mode bar and exit are host chrome).
taxonomy.packSupplies: Placeholder/hint/title keys, accent token, live-eval render of the current input, submit/exit semantics.
taxonomy.hostSupplies: The MiniAppSurface chrome, focus handling, Escape ladder, window-growth measurement.
taxonomy.note: Added at S0: the ADR-0029 slot list omitted it, but the S7 dogfooding pair (calculator, translate pad) is inexpressible without it.

taxonomy.placement: Buttons/chips in the composer toolbar row.
taxonomy.packSupplies: Action id + label key + icon spec.
taxonomy.hostSupplies: Toolbar layout, no-drag opt-out, dialogGuard for any native picker.

taxonomy.placement: Icon actions in the chat panel header (the window drag handle — contributions are no-drag).
taxonomy.packSupplies: Action id + label key + icon spec.

taxonomy.placement: Actions attached to a message/card row (e.g. per-item actions inside a rendered result).
taxonomy.packSupplies: Typed action id + label key + visibility predicate.

taxonomy.placement: Footer actions of a result/report surface (arm, export, re-run).
taxonomy.hostSupplies: Actions bar layout, dispatch, HITL wiring for arming actions.

taxonomy.placement: Status-line/strip widgets (run progress chip, live state).
taxonomy.packSupplies: A compact status renderer bound to run:* events for its own runs.
taxonomy.hostSupplies: Placement in the status strip, event subscription.

taxonomy.placement: A settings section/page beyond the auto-generated config form.
taxonomy.packSupplies: A settings panel component reading/writing only validated config keys.
taxonomy.hostSupplies: Settings shell integration, SegmentedTabs navigation, axe-clean container.

stepRules.scan: Metadata-only walk of the run root per fs.scanTraversal: includeHidden, excludeGlobs, fileCap, maxDepth. Emits the item set with fingerprints.
stepRules.classify: Deterministic-first (ADR-0029 clause 4): four ordered rule lists — veto (match → keep, hard), keep (match → keep), ask (match → ask), candidate (provisional — confirmed or demoted by compose). Evaluation order veto → keep → ask → candidate; within a list the FIRST matching rule decides and is the evidence rule (lists are author-ordered). veto/keep/ask matches finalize WITHOUT the model; candidate matches plus unmatched items form the residual handed to decide (without a decide step, a candidate match stands as candidate). (Semantics pinned at S3.)
stepRules.decide: Atomic typed questions (DecisionQuestion vocabulary) on the residual only; one engine call per item carrying all residual questions; answers + confidences land as evidence. `readContext` is the hard manifest-level allow for content excerpts; the optional `readContextWhen` condition (config signals — e.g. the user's read-context toggle) gates it per run WITHOUT a pack re-release (added at S7, append-only).
stepRules.compose: A declarative formula, never a script: runs on every model-decided item over closed signals (rule.<id> match flags + answer.<id>.* + meta/config). Evaluation order veto-guard → keepWhen → candidateWhen → askWhen; the default is ALWAYS ask (fail-closed). 'ask' is never silently promoted.
stepRules.report: Materializes the report UI schema with run data bindings.
stepRules.propose: HITL Class-B declaration: verb (apiVersion 1: 'quarantine' only), grouping key, per-item escalation, fail-closed gate (confidence threshold AND no exception hit AND no sensitive-glob match).

composeOperators.leafShape: A leaf is { signal, op, value? | valueSignal? } — 'value' is a literal (number, string, boolean for eq/ne — rule flags, or array for in/matches-any); 'valueSignal' compares against another declared signal path (e.g. meta.ageDays lt config.freshDays), enabling config-driven thresholds without scripts; 'exists' takes neither. Exactly one of value/valueSignal unless op is 'exists'. 'in' tests membership (a config array via valueSignal); 'matches' is a single glob; 'matches-any' tests against a glob LIST (literal array or a config array-of-strings via valueSignal — the exception-glob pattern). Rule signals resolve true when the rule matched, UNRESOLVED otherwise (fail-closed: comparisons on an unmatched rule read as false).

statusSemantics.paused: Budget or rate-limit exhaustion stopped cleanly; 'N items pending, resume?' is the only terminal-looking state that is resumable.
statusSemantics.interrupted: Boot reconciliation of orphaned 'running' rows; carries a resume affordance.

run.eventRules: run:started carries the pre-flight cost estimate; run:finished carries actuals (from the gateway audit); run:item streams each verdict AS IT IS COMPUTED (results stream to the UI, ADR-0029 clause 8). Renderer renders run:* events only — it never orchestrates runs (plan 26 D4).
run.fingerprint: sha256 over rootId + normalized relative path + size + mtimeMs + (contentHash iff the pipeline reads content). rootId is the resolved run-root path — verdicts NEVER transfer across roots, because deterministic rule outcomes depend on root-level state (VCS presence, sibling files), not just file bytes. contentHash is the sha256 of the same capped excerpt the questions saw (bounded IO; the verdict is cached against exactly the bytes that produced it — pinned at S3). A verdict is valid only for (fingerprint, packVersion, configHash, engineId); re-runs are cache-served; 'changed since last run' falls out of the same key. Verdicts persist as they are computed (resumable after crash/cancel/budget).
run.configHash: sha256 of canonical JSON (sorted keys, no whitespace) of the EFFECTIVE config — schema-validated, defaults merged — snapshotted and frozen at run start. Labels never participate (they live in i18n, not config).
run.budget: Estimated BEFORE the run starts (residual-estimate model) and shown in the run-start UI; exhaustion stops in 'paused' with pending count. Actual cost on the result card comes from the gateway audit rows.
run.concurrency: Runs share the engine/gateway concurrency limiter (no second limiter) through a priority wrapper that yields to interactive calls (chat/voice are never starved).

componentRules.evidence: Per-item evidence drilldown — which rule fired (rule id + matched signal values) or per-question answers + confidences. MANDATORY wherever a recommendation is rendered: a recommendation without justification is a bug (plan 26 S5).

actions.rules: run:arm binds to the pack's propose verb (apiVersion 1: quarantine) — the ADR-0029 example 'run:arm-deletion' is generalized to verb + typed action so later mutation verbs do not grow the action enum. item:override persists as user-feedback data (override capture) readable by later runs. item:restore is the Undo of quarantine. item:reveal and item:open re-validate against the RUN root with the host's open-path rails (exists; executables refused for open).

componentRules.badge: bind must be run.status — the live card has exactly one status surface.
componentRules.stat: bind must be a numeric run/totals path (never progress); the label is the i18n key live.<node.id> (required in every locale), falling back to the bind path host-side.
componentRules.progress: bind must be progress — the host resolves done/total from run events plus persisted totals; never a model of item detail (the report owns that).

liveCard.rules: Optional manifest slot liveCard: { nodes } on assessment packs (plan 28): the pack declares WHICH nodes the live run card shows, never how — rendering is host-owned, the same closed-vocabulary posture as report. A pack declaring nothing gets DEFAULT_LIVE_CARD from the SDK. Not capability-gated (every assessment pack has run); machine detail such as raw run ids stays host-side and never renders from pack data.

errors.model: Every capability call fails with one typed PackError { code, detail } — never a raw exception crossing the boundary. Host UI copy is host-localized per code (TEXT) and may interpolate detail's data keys; 'detail' is a bounded object (7E — declared keys, capped; `message` is the capped diagnostic and is never rendered raw as prose). 'retryable' is a closed enum: yes | no | after-delay | after-config-change. Resumability of a run is independent of per-call retryability.

codes.meaning: Engine/model/task unassigned, pack disabled, or surface prerequisites missing.
A keyring secret the capability resolves on is absent (e.g. the Jev engine key).
Run budget exhausted; items pending, resume offered (run remains resumable).
Engine/gateway limiter engaged; the envelope carries retryAfterMs.
Outside the run root allowlist, traversal/symlink/mount escape, or a refused root (fs.rootValidation). Never retried with the same arguments.
AbortSignal fired or the user canceled the run (the user may start a new run).
Upstream model/transport failure (5xx, timeout, malformed response after retries).
OS-level fs failure on an ALLOWED path (ENOSPC, EIO, EXDEV fallback failure) — distinct from policy denial (path-denied); the run remains resumable.
Unknown run/item id, or a quarantine artifact past its retention window. A file vanished mid-run is NOT this — it becomes 'changed-after-assessment' → ask.
Malformed capability arguments at the boundary (defense in depth; the install-time validator should have caught it earlier).

fs.rootValidation: The run root is chosen per run by the user (host picker), then validated ONCE at run start. It must not be: (a) lexically unsafe ('..' segments, NUL, empty); (b) a symlink, or containing a symlink anywhere in its own path chain that escapes the chosen root (the root is resolved to its real path first); (c) a refused root per refusedRoots; (d) a broad root — '/', the user's home itself, a drive root, or the app's userData. Nested user directories (e.g. ~/projects/foo) are fine.
fs.scanTraversal: During the walk, per entry, host-enforced: symlinks are SKIPPED (never followed, never items); a directory whose st_dev differs from the root's is a mount point — skipped; only regular files and directories enter the walk; special files (sockets, fifos, devices) are skipped. Every item path is re-resolved within the root before any read (no check-then-act gap).

refusedRoots.notes: /mnt and /media are refused as ROOTS but not as prefixes (user data under /mnt/data/... stays legal — mount points themselves are never run roots). /var is prefix-refused for v1 (server-owned trees; deliberate over-block, revisit with a real use case). Windows/macOS sets are validated with per-OS tests at S2.

fs.contentTrust: File content is untrusted input: capped (limits.contentExcerptMaxBytes), framed as data for atomic questions, and can never arm or trigger an action. The user's arming act is the structural backstop (ADR-0029 clause 6).

quarantine.layout: Mirrors origin relative paths; a batch manifest.json records origin paths, item ids, fingerprints, movedAt.
quarantine.move: Same-volume rename; cross-device (EXDEV) falls back to copy + fsync + delete (both copies exist transiently — documented). Revalidate-and-move is ONE main-side operation PER ITEM (closing the check-then-act window; a changed fingerprint drops that item to 'ask'). Batches iterate items sequentially and FAIL SOFT: already-moved items stay moved and restorable, the failing item records its typed error, the batch stops, and the run surfaces a resume/undo affordance — never all-or-nothing, never silent partial state.
quarantine.retention: Default 30 days (per-pack config), pruned on boot. Retention prune is the ONLY automatic deletion, and it deletes only quarantine copies.
quarantine.restore: item:restore reverses the move (creating missing origin parent directories); it never overwrites — an occupied origin restores to '<origin>.restore-<n>' and says so. Whole-batch undo restores in reverse order.
quarantine.permanentDelete: Never offered by packs. The only purge is a user-armed 'empty quarantine' per pack in host settings. OS trash stays an optional alternative; permanent delete is a non-goal (plan 26).

manifestFields.sendsContent: boolean — whether any question may include file content excerpts.
manifestFields.sensitiveGlobs: Pack-declared globs that are never sent to any engine and never arm a destructive action.

privacy.alwaysSent: File names, relative paths and metadata (size, mtime, extension) are ALWAYS part of question framing when the decide step runs — sendsContent governs content excerpts only. The run-start surface discloses exactly this split before the run starts.
privacy.hostBaseline: The host merges its own sensitive baseline (privacy.hostBaselineGlobs) with the pack's list — the union is enforced regardless of pack declaration. Baseline over-matching fails toward keep/never-send (safe direction); tuned with the S2 test matrix.
privacy.consistencyLint: sendsContent=false while any decide question references a content signal → invalid at validate time (the S1 CLI lint).

i18n.shape: defaultLocale + per-locale maps; UI labels resolve through the host locale with defaultLocale fallback.
i18n.scope: UI labels only (title, description, config.* labels, report.* labels, action.* labels, status.* labels). Engine question instructions are locale-free manifest data (they target the engine, not the user; they render in evidence drilldown as data).
i18n.rules: Every locale declares the same key set (validator-enforced); host UI never renders raw pack literals outside i18n resolution.

envelopeSharedFields.rules: Envelope-shared optional display metadata adopted into the mini-app kind (2026-10-19, append-only within apiVersion 1 per the evolution rule — older hosts ignore them, newer hosts accept older packs): provenance (author/license/repository) renders verbatim on cards/consent surfaces exactly like the family envelope (D25); categories come from the charter's closed browse vocabulary (extension-charter.json categories.vocabulary, mirrored here and re-synced together — dev wall 7 pins the mirror); docs is the per-extension documentation pointer (plan 34 §10.3): the fixed relative path docs/docs-tree.json, and when present the tree MUST exist beside the manifest and validate against docs-tree.schema.json's extensionDocsTree form wherever the manifest validates — a broken promise self-disables exactly like an invalid manifest. Shapes mirror extension-manifest.schema.json field-for-field.

config.shape: A JSON Schema (2020-12) subset: types string|number|boolean|array-of-string; keywords enum, default, minimum, maximum, minLength, maxLength, pattern, minItems, maxItems, title, description; additionalProperties false; depth and property caps per limits.
config.excluded: No $ref, allOf/anyOf/oneOf, object nesting beyond limits.depthMax — the host settings form renders deterministically from it.
config.rule: All user-tweakable behavior is config — guidelines, exception lists, exclusions, readContext — never a pack re-release (ADR-0029 clause 2). Config values feed classify/compose via the config.<key> signal; a configHash keys verdict validity.
config.runParams: Per-run inputs (e.g. the root path) are a separate optional schema; they never persist as config. The resolved root participates in the verdict key as rootId, not via configHash.

retention.runs: Oldest runs pruned past limits.runsRetainedPerPack; a pruned run removes its items and report data. Quarantine rows always ride their OWN retention window (never run pruning deletes quarantine copies).

install.manifest: apiVersion, identity (id/version/kind), capabilities, configSchema+defaults, privacy, run pipeline (assessment only), report schema, i18n, contributions, and (imported T2 only) the entry path.

manifestFieldMap.id: string, required, identity.idPattern, unique per install
manifestFieldMap.title: string, required in the default locale map (i18n key 'title'), <= 120 chars
manifestFieldMap.author: string, optional, envelope-shared provenance (1–120 chars) — rendered verbatim by display/consent surfaces (D25); see envelopeSharedFields
manifestFieldMap.license: string, optional, envelope-shared provenance (SPDX identifier preferred, e.g. MIT / Apache-2.0; 1–120 chars); see envelopeSharedFields
manifestFieldMap.repository: string, optional, envelope-shared provenance — https-only git URL, no userinfo, <= 512 chars; see envelopeSharedFields
manifestFieldMap.categories: array of envelope-shared browse categories, optional — closed vocabulary (envelopeSharedFields.categoriesVocabulary), <= 3 entries, unique; see envelopeSharedFields
manifestFieldMap.docs: const 'docs/docs-tree.json', optional — the per-extension documentation pointer (plan 34 §10.3): when present the tree must exist beside the manifest and validate (registration/import-enforced, exactly like an invalid manifest); see envelopeSharedFields
manifestFieldMap.icon: optional inline raster-only data-URL (png/jpeg/webp), <= limits.iconMaxBytes; SVG/XPM rejected at the same seam as app discovery (script-vector risk); absent = deterministic monogram fallback
manifestFieldMap.capabilities: array of capability ids, required, non-empty, no duplicates, no reserved/denied ids
manifestFieldMap.configSchema: JSON Schema subset, optional (surface packs may omit)
manifestFieldMap.runParams: optional JSON Schema subset describing per-run inputs (e.g. the root path); see config.runParams
manifestFieldMap.privacy: { sendsContent: boolean, sensitiveGlobs: string[], contentCapBytes?: number }, required for assessment; forbidden fields rejected for surface
manifestFieldMap.run: pipeline object (assessment ONLY): ordered steps from pipeline.steps with per-step declarations; 'propose' optional
manifestFieldMap.report: report schema object (assessment with report capability)
manifestFieldMap.liveCard: optional live run-card schema { nodes } (assessment packs, plan 28): closed badge/stat/progress subset bound to run state; absent = the SDK DEFAULT_LIVE_CARD
manifestFieldMap.contributions: slot contribution map (declarative metadata; hosts render/execute according to profile)
manifestFieldMap.entry: string, imported T2 only — a relative path to the code entry inside the bundle; never inline code. Bundled host-integrated packs carry contributions and no entry.

install.originAndDigest: Each installed pack records a sha256 content digest and origin (bundled | imported-file path + timestamp); installs are audited. Installed manifests persist in config (config.miniApps) with toolApps parity; run/verdict/quarantine data persists in the DB.
install.selfDisable: Any validation violation — unknown step/field/capability/slot, failed digest, apiVersion > current, privacy inconsistency, cross-reference break (compose referencing an undeclared rule/question id) — disables the pack with a path-precise surfaced reason. Never half-run (plan 26 D12, the AppService boot pattern).

validationPacks.pipeline: scan(root param, excludedExtensions config, includeHidden config, readContext config) → classify(veto: exception globs + sensitive; keep: recently-modified within config window, non-configurable system-ish names; candidate: build/cache patterns node_modules/dist/__pycache__/*.log/*.tmp; ask: zero-byte, unusual perms) → decide(residual: noul 'safe to delete', score 'recoverability', choice 'category') → compose(candidate = confidence ≥ config threshold ∧ no veto; below → ask) → report(stat + table + filter-bar + evidence + actions) → propose(verb quarantine, grouped by category, per-item escalation)
validationPacks.verdict: Fully expressible; exercises every Tier 0 capability except net (deliberately) and llm (optional summary note).

validationPacks.pipeline: scan → classify(missing README/license/tests, TODO density) → decide(score 'maintainability risk' on residual modules) → compose(risk bands) → report(stats + table + run:diff); NO propose step
validationPacks.verdict: Validates that propose/fs-write-quarantine are optional and report-only packs are first-class.

validationPacks.pipeline: scan → classify(deterministic rename candidates by pattern) → decide(ambiguous collisions) → compose → report(preview diff table) → propose(rename batch with undo journal) — all beyond v1
errorsExercised: invalid (reserved capability rejected at validate/install with 'requires contract apiVersion >= 2')
validationPacks.verdict: Inexpressible in v1 BY DESIGN with a precise, typed rejection — validates the reserved-capability path and the verb-generalized run:arm.
Validates the input-mode slot (added at S0) and zero-pipeline surface packs; translate's llm capability covers the sanctioned translation funnel under the task-bound-at-call-time rule.

s0GapResolutions: ADDED compose operator 'matches-any' (S1, append-only within apiVersion 1) — glob-LIST membership (literal array or config array-of-strings via valueSignal); the exception-glob config pattern is inexpressible with single-glob 'matches' (r2.3).
ADDED slot 'input-mode' — the ADR-0029 list of 7 could not express the calculator/translate takeover surfaces the plan itself mandates migrating (S7).
ADDED reserved capability 'fs-write-mutate' (apiVersion >= 2) — batch-renamer is inexpressible via fs-write-quarantine alone; v1 rejects it with a typed reason instead of an unknown-capability error.
ADDED error codes 'io', 'not-found', 'invalid' — quarantine ENOSPC, post-retention restore, and boundary-validation failures had no code in the ADR's seven.
GENERALIZED 'run:arm-deletion' → 'run:arm' + propose.verb — action enum stays closed as mutation verbs evolve.
FIXED run status/event vocabulary incl. 'paused' (resumable budget stop) and 'interrupted' (boot reconciliation) — the ADR named the behavior but no enum.
FIXED host-owned sensitive-glob baseline merged with pack declarations (union enforced).
ADDED rootId to the verdict key (r2) — verdicts never transfer across roots; deterministic rule outcomes depend on root-level state, so the ADR's bare relative-path fingerprint was unsafe.
PINNED configHash (r2) — canonical JSON of effective config, frozen at run start; labels excluded.
SPLIT root validation from scan traversal (r2) — mount-point skip, symlink skip, regular-files-only are per-entry scan rules; the S2 escape matrix derives from both halves.
ADDED kill switches (r2) — master + per-pack + armed-batch abort semantics.
MADE ADR-0015 Tier 1 floor explicit for proposals (r2) — idempotent resolve, conflict rebase-or-reject, notification fanout; per-item-atomic fail-soft batches.
NAMESPACED slot contribution ids '<packId>:<id>' + fixed multi-pack composition order (r2).
NORMALIZED error 'retryable' to a closed enum (r2); resumability is separate from retryability.
ADDED privacy.alwaysSent (r2) — metadata is always in question framing; disclosed at run start.

ADDED append-only minor-evolution rule, install id-collision/upgrade semantics, item:open action, sha256 digest pin, restore-creates-parents, run-retention pruning semantics, and the manifestFieldMap (r2).
